data: Australia's first satellite, WRESAT (1967), and Britain's Black Arrow launch of Prospero (1971)

Facts from the Wikipedia articles on the RAAF Woomera Range Complex, WRESAT, Prospero and Woomera Launch Area 5, and Encyclopedia Astronautica (Woomera and LA8 pages). Coordinates are the Launch Area 5B pad (Black Arrow, Prospero) as mapped in OpenStreetMap; Launch Area 8 has no precise published position. The range is now run by the RAAF.

Woomera is a rocket range in the South Australian desert, about 450 km north-west of Adelaide, set up in 1946-47 for the Anglo-Australian long-range weapons project. Two of its launch areas reached orbit. From Launch Area 8, a US Redstone with Sparta upper stages put WRESAT, a 45 kg satellite built by the Weapons Research Establishment, into a near-polar orbit on 29 November 1967: Australia's first satellite. From Launch Area 5B, a Black Arrow carried Prospero into orbit on 28 October 1971, the first British satellite launched on a British rocket; the programme was cancelled afterwards. The orbital launch areas are disused, but the range, now run by the RAAF, is still used for defence testing; its prohibited area covers 122,188 km2.
